items.english: The fallen Kotora quietly took it. No sooner had she drawn it than she drove it suddenly into O-Tetsu's side. O-Tetsu's scream was a single cry.
notes: Kept flat as written: one cry, no death stated.

items.english: "It is a woman's pride. I am Take-wari Kotora, after all. Come, Danna-sama, I shall go with you to Edo."
notes: Kept Danna-sama and troupe name as claimed identity; no build-up added.

items.english: She wiped the bloodied blade on O-Tetsu's sleeve, put it back in its sheath, and handed it back to him.
What could never have been settled in one way or two was simply cut through by Kotora. Ryujiro could only marvel at the strangeness of fate.

Mr ○○○○○, famed until mid-Meiji as the Metropolitan Police's foremost old detective in arrests, was none other than the later self of this Isogai Ryujiro. His former wife was none other than Kotora, though she is said to have died of illness early in Meiji. Whether Ryujiro ever received the secret transmission of Happo Makigumo from Jinpusai, on that point, regrettably, nothing has come down.
notes: Kept circles and flat closing shrug as written; names in romanisation without addition.
